Question 3 of 3 · P-12 and P-33Do the library's other components block only the step at which walk runs the checker?

The briefing

The distance is the number of errors that the compiled checker reports on the library's core, twelve components. The fourteen components are those twelve and the two that List imports, CovariantCollection and OneShotFlag. Climb batch 22c adds the two to the distance. The library has 40 other components outside the twelve, 38 outside the fourteen. Checked once, they hold 624 component errors, at least 92 api errors and 25 crashes. The step at which walk runs the checker comes after the switch-over. Walk, the interpreter, then runs the compiled type checker on its own programs (P-12). The foundations review ruled that the other components block that later step, not the switch-over. Each is cleared before that step, or before the first program that needs it. P-33, as corrected on 29 October, says that the other components are not part of phase 3, and that F-290 counts their errors. It does not say whether the switch-over waits for them. When you read P-33's new text, at 07:34 UTC on 29 October (08:34 your time), the held list records your words: “during the tenets review they discovered a part of the library that was not counted and decided to clear it per part as the need arises; the coordinator failed to record that decision”. That reads as the default, and the queue still holds the question open. No text of the language speaks to this. It is a question of the order of the work, and the record's grounds are the review's ruling and P-12. MicroGPT imports some of these components. Checked alone, System gives 2 errors, File 4, FileSupport 24 and FortressAst 1.

What climb batch 22c does with your answer

No task of climb batch 22c changes with your answer. Its task that adds List's two imports to the distance makes the distance cover the fourteen under either answer. The batch record files the other components as left out: each is to be cleared before the step at which walk runs the checker, or before the first program that needs it. That is the default. Under the other answer, the batch stays the same, and the switch-over's exit widens to the whole library. The 624 errors and 25 crashes then come first, in batches that no probe has measured.

The entry's text

Your answer changes no entry text: P-12 and P-33, as they now read, hold under either answer.

P-12, the current text

P-12 After the switch-over, walk runs the compiled type checker on its programs, and then uses the static coercions that the checker inserts. The curator wants the checker usable on the programs that walk runs. Today fortress typecheck checks a program only against the compiler's prelude, so it is no check of walk's programs (F-9 holds this fact). Walk is not changed for this before the switch-over. After it, walk runs the checker on its programs and so gains their static types; F-9 and F-290 say what walk and the library lack for that step. Walk then uses the static coercions that the checker inserts, in place of its choice on the run-time value (P-59, walk's choice of coercions until the switch-over).

P-33, the current text

P-33 The work toward microGPT compiled follows the phases, in the order that the curator approved. These phases are steps of the work, not the compiler's phases, and they are numbered 3 to 6, after two earlier ones. Phase 3 ends when the compiled checker reports no error on the apis and components of the interpreter's library that the distance to the switch-over counts (F-53 defines the distance, says what it counts and holds its value). The library's other components are not part of phase 3; F-290 counts their errors. Phase 4, the switch-over: first the natives, the library's builtinPrimitive bindings made to run on the compiled path, then the compiled path reads the interpreter's library and the compiler's prelude is deleted; phase 5, microGPT compiles: its static types, the array design and the code generator's open gaps; phase 6, microGPT runs fast. Code-generator work goes on beside that order, under either library (P-37). Row 320, an api implemented by a component of another name does not link, is part of the switch-over's design.

The options

  1. Default. They block only the step at which walk runs the checker. Each is cleared before that step, or before the first program that needs it, such as microGPT's imports.

    It gives up: The switch-over then happens while parts of the library still fail the checker. A compiled program that imports one of them waits until it is cleared.

  2. They are cleared before the switch-over.

    It gives up: The switch-over waits for 624 component errors, at least 92 api errors and 25 crashes to be cleared, in a number of batches that no probe has measured.

- Each section is one entry. It gives the entry's text as it reads now, the text drafted to replace it, the words removed and added, and in a few plain sentences what is false, why, and what the change alters in the work.
- Nothing here is applied. POSITIONS is his text, and he says yes or no to each section. At his yes, `explorations/coordinator/tools/record.py set` writes the new text, with a note that names this file's section; the tool keeps the old line in `POSITIONS-history.md`.
- The drafts follow his rules for a correction (`coordinator` skill, `references/record.md`): change as little as the fact needs; a false sentence is corrected; a reason that is not his goes to the history, and his meaning stays; no date goes into an entry.
- Where the record does not settle a text, the section holds a question with its options in place of a text. Two such questions are on P-42: its example (section 1) and its word "functions" (section 12).

**Old text**

> - P-146 **In a self-typed trait, the compiled checker types `self` in the method bodies as also being the implementing type.** A self-typed trait is a trait `C[\X\]` whose parameter `X` extends `C[\X\]`, such as `Integral[\I extends Integral[\I\]\]`. In its method bodies, `self` has the type `C[\X\] & X`. The method signatures keep the plain trait type, because the proofs of the POPL 2019 paper on multiple dispatch (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu) assume that no declared type holds a type parameter inside an intersection. Only the overloading check's exclusion test reads `self` in a signature as `C[\X\] & X` (P-157).
